public_payload.normalized_proposition: The author estimates there is maybe $22 billion of demand right now outside Anthropic and OpenAI.

statement.excerpt: Right now, I estimate that there’s maybe $22 billion of demand outside of Anthropic and OpenAI.

our_interpretation: The preceding comparison to annual compute demand makes the ordinary reading approximately $22 billion per year of current AI compute demand from customers other than the two named labs.
Treat this as an approximate estimate, not an exact dollar threshold or a hard upper bound.
Use the latest completed calendar quarter with public reporting before the post, April through June 2026, as the measurement window for the current annualized spending pace.
Measure purchases of AI compute once at the customer-to-provider boundary. Exclude the two labs’ purchases and avoid adding downstream AI application revenue to upstream compute spending.
The statement does not make clear how internally operated compute should be valued.
criteria.support_condition: A reasonably comprehensive estimate of annualized AI compute spending by other customers, using a consistent definition and the selected reporting period, centers near $22 billion with uncertainty compatible with that approximation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable comprehensive estimate or defensible lower bound places the annualized total materially away from $22 billion, beyond measurement uncertainty and ordinary rounding.
